These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize unit prices with to_money: Wrap raw line unit prices with ledgerly.money.to_money before multiplying by quantity, and seed sums with the ZERO constant from ledgerly.money, as line_total and invoice_total do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

candidate.content: Always pass monetary inputs through `to_money` from `ledgerly.money` before storing them on models; it rejects floats with a `float_amount` BillingError and returns a Decimal. Compare against `ZERO` from `ledgerly.money` for sign checks.

item.title: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes
item.content: Signal domain failures by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with the established codes: `invalid_state` for wrong invoice status, `invalid_quantity` for bad quantities, `negative_amount` for negative money.

item.title: Reject bools and non-int quantities explicitly
item.content: When validating integer quantities, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(quantity, bool)`) before the `isinstance(quantity, int)` check, since `True`/`False` are ints in Python and would otherwise pass.
